frame: analysed papers with a reference section read (>= 2000 chars) and no cross-regime edge in the union network
method: largest share of a target title's content words inside one 60-word window of the reference section, any order; deliberately not v3's id/prefix matching

positive_control.design: run the same scanner over papers that DO have a known cross-regime edge, and see whether it finds that edge
positive_control.note: the scanner is not silently too strict

verdicts.citing: Gated Coordination for Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration in Minecraft Game
verdicts.why: The window is the paper's own body text about separating private execution memory from public coordination records, not a reference entry. It shares context/execution/agents with the target title by subject matter. 'Integrity' does not appear.

verdicts.why: Matched 'retrieval augmented generation' inside a DIFFERENT reference (Kim and Diaz, fair ranking in RAG). 'Corrective' absent.

verdicts.citing: MemLineage: Lineage-Guided Enforcement for LLM Agent Memory

what_this_does_not_cover: citations to other-regime work that is NOT in the analysed set -- those never counted toward the rate in the first place
precision. This checks whether the matcher MISSED citations, not whether the 138 edges it found are real
the 586 evidenced negatives that were not drawn

short_section_census.why: The sampling frame originally dropped papers whose reference section came out under 2000 characters, on the assumption that a short section means a truncated extraction. That assumption was wrong, so instead of excluding them all 14 were read in full -- a census, not a sample.
short_section_census.completeness_test: For each paper: compare the highest in-text citation marker in the body against the number of entries captured, and measure how much PDF text follows the reference section. A truncated extraction shows markers above the last captured entry, or text after the section. All 14 show neither: the markers stop at or below the entries captured, and 0 characters follow.
short_section_census.verdict: all 14 are complete short bibliographies -- 4 to 14 references, from short workshop and conference papers -- not truncations
short_section_census.cross_regime_scan: Re-scanned at a LOWER threshold (0.50) against every analysed title of both regimes. 8 cross-regime candidates surfaced across the 14; all 8 are the same generic-phrase collision: 'retrieval augmented generation' inside the Lewis et al. RAG reference matching PoisonedRAG / TrojanRAG / BadRAG / Corrective RAG / ConflictRAG, and 'agent ... reinforcement learning' across the Voyager and Reflexion entries. Every one is missing the title's distinguishing word.
